formal.statement: ∀ (n : ℤ), Int.fib (2 * n) = Int.fib n * (2 * Int.fib (n + 1) - Int.fib n)

notes:
Closed in-tree. No induction was needed -- the prior lane's sizing ('~200-250 lines, no new device') held once the subtraction bridge existed. Route: Int.fib_add n n gives fib(n+n) = fib(n-1)*fib n + fib n*fib(n+1); the new bridge fib_pred_eq_sub (built for this lane, general form `a+b=c |- b=c-a`, named eq_sub_of_add_eq_left) rewrites fib(n-1) as fib(n+1)-fib(n) via Int.fib_rec at n-1; the rest is ring algebra (mul_comm, Int.mul_sub, left_distrib, and a small `(x-y)+x = (x+x)-y` rearrangement) to fold the result into the `2*fib(n+1)-fib n` shape, plus a `2*t = t+t` helper (mul_two_eq_add_self) to bridge the index `2*n` to `n+n`.

The real cost was not the algebra but a direction bug: `Int.isymm(a, b, h)` requires `h : Eq(a,b)` and returns `Eq(b,a)`; five call sites across this lane's new helpers passed the arguments in the wrong order relative to the hypothesis actually in hand. Every individual sub-proof still type-checked in isolation against its own (also-backwards) declared expectation, so a concrete `n=3` instantiation test passed cleanly on the first attempt; the mismatch surfaced only once the pieces were chained with a genuinely free `n`, diagnosed by re-deriving the construction against a free variable pushed into an explicit LocalContext and checking each named intermediate one at a time.
